install.title: Install Habit tracker
install.intro: To use it as an app (and, later on, to get notifications) add it to your Home Screen and always open it from its icon.
install.step1: In Safari, tap the Share button
install.step3: Open the app from the new icon
install.safariOnly: On iPhone this has to be done in Safari.

stats.title: Stats
stats.hint: Week and month: days done out of every day due in the whole period. Total: out of the days due up to today. Today counts once you complete it (for negative habits, once the day is over).

plant.wiltedHint: Complete it on the next due day and it will revive.
plant.bloom: In bloom! Keep it up to keep it that way.

heatmap.read: Each square is a day and each column a week (Monday on top). The stronger the color, the more you did; for quantitative habits, according to the amount. Very light squares are days it wasn’t due, and the outline marks today. For negative habits clean days are colored and relapses show in red.
heatmap.purpose: See your consistency over the last weeks at a glance, spot gaps and keep the chain going.
heatmap.ideal: Daily or almost daily habits: meditate, drink water, no smoking.

calendar.read: A whole month. Filled circle: done. Outlined circle: partial (quantitative) or pending today. Grey: missed. Faint number: not due that day. In the detail view you can move between months.
calendar.purpose: Review specific months and find which weekdays are hardest for you.
calendar.ideal: Habits on specific days or X times a week: gym, classes, cleaning the house.

ring.read: The ring fills with the days done out of every day due this week (Monday to Sunday) or this month, as you choose: a 4-times-a-week habit only reaches 100% with the fourth. Below it you see how many you’ve done.
ring.purpose: A short, clear goal: close the ring this week.
ring.ideal: Any habit, especially non-daily ones: reading on weekdays, calling family.

bars.read: Each bar is the amount logged that day and the dashed line is your goal. Strong color: you reached the goal; lighter: you fell short. With 30 days it’s drawn as a line.
bars.purpose: See how much you do, not just whether you do it, and whether you’re trending up or down.
bars.ideal: Quantitative habits: glasses of water, steps, minutes of study.

days_since.read: The big number is the consecutive clean days you’ve already completed: today counts once it’s over. Below it, your record.
days_since.purpose: Watching the number grow is a reason not to start from zero again.
days_since.ideal: Negative habits: no smoking, no soda, no nail biting.

marble_jar.read: Every time you complete it, a marble drops into the jar; for quantitative habits, one per amount you choose (e.g. 1 marble = 1 km), adding up across days. Missing never removes marbles. If you fill it early, you’ll see the extra marbles. When the period ends (week, month, quarter or year) the jar goes to the shelf, which shows the last 12.
marble_jar.purpose: Watch what you’ve built up grow without fear of losing it: one bad day doesn’t spoil the jar.
marble_jar.ideal: Yes/no or quantitative habits that don’t need to be daily: gym, kilometers run, books read.

plant.read: The plant grows with the days you complete out of your last 14 due days: sprout at 3, young plant at 6, plant at 9 and flower at 12. A new habit starts as a seed and grows day by day. Miss 3 due days in a row and it wilts, but it never dies: it revives as soon as you complete it again. For quantitative habits, a day counts if you reach the goal.
plant.purpose: Reward recent consistency: what counts is how you’re doing now, not months ago.
plant.ideal: Yes/no or quantitative habits you want to keep alive: practicing an instrument, studying, watering the plants.
